sections.heading: Adapt when backing changes
sections.content: Kapoor had planned to build Design Nation within an existing Princeton organization, which had funding, resources, and expertise. When it was skeptical the project could be funded, she went from expecting those supports to having none and needing to build the conference from the ground up. She said it was important to keep chasing the goal even without formal backing and to be adaptable about resourcing.

sections.heading: Shift effort to the current bottleneck
sections.content: She described changing how she allocated her own time: speakers might stop being the priority if fundraising became more important, or creating a hype landing page might matter most to make a scrappy, few-person student organization seem more legitimate. To build support, she cold-emailed many people and executives using her .edu address; designers who related to the problem offered to help.
